---
title: "check-quarto-links.yml"
---

Fail when a tracked `.qmd`, `.md`, or `.Rmd` file links to a page that does
not exist, such as `[Week 6](week-06-logistic-regression.qmd)` after that
page was renamed.

## Why a separate check

**Quarto does not fail the render.**
It prints `WARN: Unable to resolve link target: chapters/week-06-logistic-regression.qmd`
and publishes the page with the dead link, so a green render proves nothing
about links between pages.

**[`check-links.yml`](check-links.qmd) does not see them either.**
lychee picks a parser by file extension and reads a `.qmd` as plain text, so it
extracts only absolute URLs from one and never checks a relative link.
Measured with lychee 0.24.2, the version `lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0`
installs (2026-09-28): a `.qmd` holding two dead relative links reports
`0 Errors`, with or without `--default-extension md`.
The same file renamed to `.md` reports both.

A render-log alternative already exists:
[`preview.yml`](preview.qmd) and [`quarto-publish.yml`](quarto-publish.qmd)
accept `forbid-log-patterns: 'Unable to resolve link target'`.
This check needs no render, runs in seconds, and names the source file and
line rather than the rendered page.

## What it checks

Every Markdown inline link (`[text](target)`, including one whose `](` falls on
the next line), reference definition (`[label]: target`), and raw HTML `href`
or `src` in each tracked file matching `globs`, whose target ends in one of
`target-extensions`.
A target resolves from the linking file's directory, or, when it starts with
`/`, from the Quarto project directory (the nearest ancestor holding
`_quarto.yml`).

Not checked, by design:

- links inside fenced code blocks, code spans, and HTML comments;
- URLs with a scheme (`https:`, `mailto:`), `//` URLs, and `#anchor`-only
  links;
- targets built from a shortcode or an inline expression, such as
  `{{< meta >}}`;
- whether the `#anchor` part of a link exists on the target page.

**Included files resolve from the page that includes them.**
Quarto splices a `{{< include _sub/_part.qmd >}}` file into the including page
before it resolves links, so a link in `_part.qmd` is written relative to the
page, not to `_sub/`.
The check accepts a link that resolves from the file's own directory or from
any page that includes it, directly or through other includes.
A `_`-prefixed file that nothing includes, such as an outtake kept for reuse,
is skipped and named in the log, since Quarto never renders it and there is no
page to resolve its links from.

**Whole tree, not the pull request's diff.**
A link that went dead when another pull request renamed its target is still a
live defect, and the pull request that renamed the page is the one that did not
touch the link.

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | string | `'*.qmd *.md *.Rmd'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked source files to scan (recursive). |
| `target-extensions` | string | `'.qmd, .md, .Rmd, .ipynb'` | Extensions of link targets to verify. |
| `paths-ignore` | string | `''` | Comma- or newline-separated globs (`*`, `?`, `**`) of source files to skip. |
| `fail` | boolean | `true` | Fail the job on a finding (else warn only). The composite reads it fail-closed: only an explicit `false` opts out. |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
name: Check Quarto links
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-quarto-links.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/'
    #   target-extensions: '.qmd, .md'
    #   fail: false
```

See `check-quarto-links.yml` in
[`examples/`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/tree/main/examples)
for the full caller stub.
